investigation.title: Northwind Logistics — invoice totals after release 4.12
investigation.escalationText: Meridian reports that invoice totals have been wrong since release 4.12, our finance team is blocked, and we have not had a reply to four messages. Please explain what happened and when this will be fixed.
investigation.plan:
Meridian (Northwind Logistics) reports invoice totals wrong since release 4.12; finance blocked; four messages unanswered. The event store shows related Jira/Slack activity around MER-87 (UTC date handling change) and MER-101 (reported totals/timeline issues), with a claimed fix scheduled and then marked resolved, but QA still failing. This plan tests causal links, communication gaps, and scope of the problem.

Hypotheses to test:
- The MER-87 timezone change (switch invoice date handling to UTC) is the root cause of the wrong invoice totals reported in MER-101. — test: Review MER-87 change details (diff, deployment date) and MER-101 description; correlate timing with 4.12 release; examine test results and QA failures that reference MER-87.; falsify: If MER-87 change was deployed after the first report of wrong totals, or if MER-101 issues are unrelated to date handling (e.g., calculation errors), then this hypothesis is false.
- The fix for MER-101 was not actually deployed or effective, as evidenced by QA still failing on the Sep 24 build and the issue being marked Resolved prematurely. — test: Check deployment logs for the Sep 24 release; review QA test results mentioned in Slack; verify if MER-101 status change to Resolved was accompanied by verification steps or customer confirmation.; falsify: If QA failures were resolved before the Sep 24 build, or if the fix was deployed and verified by Meridian, then this hypothesis is false.
- The lack of response to Meridian's four messages is due to internal communication breakdowns, such as Lin Chen being on leave without handoff. — test: Search for Meridian's inbound messages and internal discussion about responses; check if any outbound communication was sent after each inbound; review handoff processes for MER-101.; falsify: If evidence shows Meridian received timely responses, or if the messages were never received, then this hypothesis is false.

Source plan:
- jira: Retrieve full issue histories for MER-87, MER-101, and any linked issues; focus on status transitions, comments, and change logs; look for references to 4.12, timezone, and invoice totals.
- slack: Search meridian-billing channel for all messages mentioning Meridian, MER-101, totals, fix, and response; also check direct messages if accessible; look for mentions of unanswered client messages.
- email: Search for emails from or to Meridian (Northwind Logistics) regarding invoice totals, 4.12, and escalations; check sent items for replies to the four messages; identify any unanswered threads.

Seed terms: MER-101, MER-87, MER-102, MER-104, 4.12, meridian-billing, invoice, totals, wrong, timezone, UTC, fix, release, build, nightly, export, dependency, status, resolved, open

People to look at: Marcus Webb, Dana Okoro, Lin Chen, Priya Nair

Focus window: 2024-09-01 → 2024-09-30

Unknowns to keep open:
- The exact content of Meridian's four unanswered messages and when they were sent.
- Whether any internal replies were drafted but not sent.
- The deployment date and contents of release 4.12.
- Whether the Sep 24 release included the fix and if it was verified.
- The current status of MER-101 and whether Meridian has confirmed any resolution.
- Whether other clients are affected by the same timezone change.
- Who was responsible for responding to Meridian while Lin Chen was on leave.
- Whether the MER-101 resolution was based on internal testing or customer confirmation.
